audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may receive acquisition benefits without paying acquisition costs
audit_findings.magnitude: $137.530 million in 2025 and $252.746 million in 2024; 27.3% and 50.2% of $503.9 million anchor OE, respectively
audit_findings.mechanism: Forecast growth and the reinvestment deduction within owner earnings
audit_findings.evidence: Net sales increased for the year ended December 31, 2025 primarily due to an increase in organic sales and a benefit from acquisitions.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved modeling possibility, not a demonstrated error: acquisitions supplied 2.7% of 2025 sales growth, but the record does not establish that the 4% base forecast requires continued acquisitions. The historical outlays are large relative to anchor OE, so including acquired growth without its required acquisition spending could materially overstate operating value.
audit_findings.action: Separate organic and acquired earnings contributions, demonstrate that 4% growth is supportable organically under the modeled reinvestment assumptions, and rerun any acquisition-supported scenario using a normalized acquisition cost net of acquired OE.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded pension claims may not be captured by owner earnings or the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $38.738 million filed 2025 funded deficit, equal to 0.50% of $7.725 billion base equity value or $0.70 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Potential bridge deduction or normalization of pension cash payments in OE
audit_findings.evidence: Pension plans are funded except for a domestic non-qualified pension plan for certain key employees and certain foreign plans.
audit_findings.explanation: The pension deficit is demonstrated, but omission from value is not established because pension expense is included in earnings and future cash payments may already affect OE. Even treating the entire filed deficit as an additional equity claim would reduce base value only from $139.51 to about $138.81 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $38.738 million funded deficit, pension expense, contributions, and benefit payments to the OE calculation; deduct only the portion not already captured.

audit_findings.title: Deferred-compensation liability is an unbridged senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $28.052 million filed at June 30, 2026, equal to 0.36% of $7.725 billion base equity value or $0.51 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Potential senior-claim deduction in the equity bridge or future cash settlement through OE
audit_findings.evidence: The deferred compensation liability is the Company’s obligation under its executive deferred compensation plan.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability and its absence from the stated bridge are demonstrated, but the record does not establish whether matching assets or future OE capture the settlement. Even a full unoffset deduction would lower base value only to about $139.00 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Identify any dedicated offsetting assets and trace expected settlements through forecast OE; subtract the net unfunded amount only if it is not otherwise captured.

audit_findings.title: Cash may not be fully excess or distributable at face value
audit_findings.magnitude: $242.443 million total June 2026 cash, including $181.012 million held internationally; complete removal equals 3.14% of base equity value or $4.38 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Dollar-for-dollar cash addition in the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the Company had cash of $308,789, of which $294,130 was held by international subsidiaries.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the cash is excess and distributable is unresolved. Nevertheless, the maximum bridge exposure is bounded by the entire $242.443 million balance: removing all of it would reduce base value from $139.51 to about $135.13 per share, still far below the $276.44 market price and therefore not capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Determine June 2026 operating-cash needs, jurisdictional location, restrictions, and withholding leakage, then replace gross cash with net distributable excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Non-recurring non-operating income may remain in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $9.397 million filed pre-tax bucket, equal to 1.9% of $503.9 million anchor OE; a full dollar-for-dollar anchor reduction computes to about $139.6 million or $2.52 per share of base value
audit_findings.mechanism: One-time income potentially included in anchor OE and capitalized through forecast operating value
audit_findings.evidence: Other income primarily relates to non-recurring items and non-operating gains and losses.
audit_findings.explanation: The non-recurring income bucket is demonstrated, but its inclusion in the $503.9 million anchor is not established without the OE reconciliation. Even conservatively treating the full pre-tax amount as an OE overstatement would reduce base value by only about 1.8% and would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $9.397 million components through net income and the OE adjustments, remove any included non-recurring gains, and rerun the anchor if necessary.

audit_findings.title: Asbestos exposure is an unquantified contingent claim
audit_findings.mechanism: Potential uninsured settlement or judgment would reduce OE when paid or require a senior-claim deduction in the bridge
audit_findings.evidence: The claimants in the asbestos cases seek compensatory and punitive damages, in most cases for unspecified amounts.
audit_findings.explanation: This is not a demonstrated valuation error. The June 2026 filing reports approximately 701 claimants, declining claim counts, historically favorable resolutions, and only immaterial settlements, but it provides no reasonably possible uninsured loss range. The exposure may affect value, while the supplied record cannot establish its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain booked reserves, insurance limits and exclusions, cost-sharing terms, post-filing claim developments, and any reasonably possible uninsured loss range; rerun the bridge only if a supportable net exposure emerges.
